summary: INSERT adds new rows to a table.
points: INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES (1, 'a') adds one row. Naming the columns makes it clear and safe.
List several value sets, separated by commas, to add many rows at once.
Columns you leave out get NULL, or their default.
INSERT INTO table SELECT ... copies rows from a query.

example.explanation: This example adds a row and shows the result. Examples run on a temporary copy, so nothing is saved.
